$schema_note: Companion to HANDOFF.md. Grades: A primary source, B published secondary, C derivable arithmetic, D judgement, F invented (do not propagate).
subject: Bloomfield, Connecticut - truck parking / industrial outdoor storage development
status: feasibility analysis, self-audited, incomplete by design

headline.conclusion: The deal as scoped does not work. The reason is solid. The recommended fix (buy scale) rests on an assumption since shown to be probably wrong.
headline.strongest_finding: Negative leverage - yield on cost 2.68-4.36% against a 7.25% debt rate in all scenarios.
headline.weakest_link: The highest-elasticity input (blended revenue per stall, |e|=1.67) is grade F.

reduced_model.test_0_leverage_sign: YoC vs interest rate; if YoC < rate, leverage is negative
reduced_model.test_1_marginal_unit: m = (R-c)*12 - D*LTC*k*v ; if m <= 0 no scale ever works
reduced_model.test_2_scale_threshold: N* = B/m where B = F + D*LTC*k*PHI

findings.finding: Negative leverage in all three scenarios
Fixed costs are 56-81% of capital cost
A marginal stall is self-financing (m=+$1,647/yr, S2)
The retrofit has the highest DSCR ceiling (7.05x vs 3.48x)
P(clearing 1.25x at 10 acres) = 7.2%; 50% crossing near 18 acres

challenge_register.claim_under_attack: Scale fixes the deal - build 14-18+ acres
challenge_register.defect: Occupancy is held constant at 88% while stall count triples. Occupancy is an output of demand vs supply, not an independent input.
challenge_register.illustrative_sensitivity: 10% occupancy decay per doubling pushes the 1.25x crossing past 30 acres; 20% decay removes it entirely
challenge_register.resolve_by: catchment demand estimate - truck volumes on I-91/I-84 within 30 minutes, Hartford MSA fleet domiciles, CTDOT overnight deficit localised
rate survey of secured 53ft stalls within 15 miles; ~1 week
challenge_register.if_it_fails: below ~$300 no Bloomfield site size rescues it; move markets

challenge_register.claim_under_attack: This is a per-stall retail parking operation
challenge_register.never_compared: bulk NNN lease of the yard to a single fleet or 3PL tenant
challenge_register.why: eliminates ~$182/stall/month operating overhead, lease-up risk and management intensity at lower rent per acre; Hartford bulk yard leases noted at ~$35-55k/acre/yr but never modelled

challenge_register.never_modelled: trailer-only drop-lot storage - ~55ft stalls, 25-30% more per acre, no driver amenities, lower rates

challenge_register.alternative: For single-purpose operating-business-like collateral it may be binary. If no lender takes it, DSCR is moot.

challenge_register.defect: Allocates half a drive aisle to every stall; assumes uniform double-loaded rows. Real layouts have perimeter rows, turning bulbs, pull-through stalls.
No usable comp. Elasticity only 0.38 and no land price alone rescues the deal, so lower priority than it looks - but still a fabricated anchor.

challenge_register.claim_under_attack: Entitlement is a cost and schedule item
challenge_register.defect: Bloomfield TPZ has treated outdoor storage as not permitted as a principal use (grade A, meeting minutes). Model carries $85k legal and 14 months but NO probability of refusal.

unexamined_territory: Demand - no catchment analysis, competitive supply inventory, or seasonality
Competitive response - CTDOT adding ~180 free public spaces by ~2030
Lease-up duration as a function of programme size (6-month reserve assumed regardless; sourced guidance says ~36 months to stabilization)
Downside floor - alternative industrial land value if the use fails
Tax abatement and municipal industrial incentives
Interest rate path and refinance risk - single fixed 7.25% throughout
Cargo theft and liability tail - garagekeepers named, exposure not stress-tested
Operator comparables - no actual operator P&L obtained; the opex stack is constructed, not observed
Environmental exposure bounding under CT Release-Based Remediation
known_defects: Six parameters graded F used in a model presented with cent-level precision
Cost-per-stall chosen as denominator without testing $/acre, which would have surfaced the bulk-lease alternative earlier
Cap-rate valuation applied to an operating business - wrong instrument
Only three grade-A facts in the entire analysis: mill rate, assessment ratio, zoning posture
next_work_ordered: Rate survey (C-2) - one week, falsifies the dominant input
Catchment demand estimate (C-1) - determines whether the scale recommendation is valid at all
Zoning pre-application meeting (C-8) - converts a binary risk into a known one
Only then revisit site selection and retrofit-at-scale
